chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife after he had lain with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. He said, 'This is not a divorce.'

I said, 'May I be your ransom, how is the Sunnah divorce?' He said, 'He divorces her when she becomes pure from her menses, before he lies with her, with two just witnesses, as Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said in His Book. If he contradicts that, it is referred back to the Book of Allah.'

I said to him, 'But he divorced her while pure, without sexual intercourse, with one man and two women.' He said, 'The testimony of women is not valid in divorce, but their testimony is valid with men in blood (diyah) if they witness it.'

I said, 'If he witnesses two men who are Naasibi (opponents of the Ahl al-Bayt) regarding the divorce, does it count as a divorce?' He said, 'Whoever is born upon the natural disposition (fitrah), his testimony is accepted in divorce after you know goodness from him.'

key_terms.طَلاَقُ السُّنَّةِ: Sunnah divorce (divorce performed according to the Prophet's method)
key_terms.غَشِيَهَا: He lay with her / consummated the marriage
key_terms.نَاصِبِيَّيْنِ: Two Naasibi (opponents of the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for a valid Sunnah divorce according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the precise conditions for a valid Sunnah divorce, emphasizing that it must occur during a period of purity (tuhr) prior to sexual intercourse, accompanied by two just witnesses. The narration further clarifies the jurisprudential distinction that while women's testimony is accepted for blood money (diyah), it is not valid for divorce, and establishes that Naasibi individuals are eligible as witnesses provided their goodness is verified.
